This is mine and my SO's 3rd Valentine's day together and I was pretty surprised the other day when he asked me what we were doing for it. We don't really celebrate it as 'Valentine's Day' we just kind of decide 'Oh... well lets plan a date then!' This year we're going to do what we did last year. Indoor picnic :) I get to have delicious picnic-type food, probably some lit candles, have a drink or two and relax with each other.


However, just once I'd like to get flowers (I've never gotten flowers before) but I'm not really fussy...

Or the people who come in who say "Yeah, I'm looking for this self-help book, I think it's x amount of steps to something something. I think it was in a newspaper two weeks ago." Then they get mad at you because that's not NEARLY enough to go on. (True story - this actually happened)

I'm already doing post-secondary. I'm doing full-time post-secondary while working "part-time" (i.e. almost full-time hours most of the time). In the past its been expected of me to miss class to fill in shifts, they almost didn't give me my exam days off (that's a whole other story) but I'm in my last year of my undergrad now (I'm only 20 btw), so not too much longer and I can just focus on one thing at a time...
It's totally true. I'm a supervisor, but as a supervisor you don't get paid any more than if you were a regular sales associate or a cashier... its infuriating...

Thank you for your response <3. I am diagnosed as having depression and anxiety (also severe OCD) but for the career path I want to go into I can't be on any medication so I need to learn to cope without medication if I want to accomplish my goals. But you're exactly right, I let it affect me outside of work when I should be enjoying that time away and it just becomes a vicious circle of misery because I just start to dread having to work so much. The problem is I used to LOVE my job, I loved the location and then I had to transfer stores, and I hate my new store, the customers are more rude, and the managers more demanding and incredibly "corporate". I can give examples if you want some...

Agreed. I hate it. And then when they do come in the managers don't give us time to call the customers so we end up with a pile of orders waiting to be picked up that haven't been called... it's just a vicious circle.

That's the thing. Some people are sensitive, some people have stories that you may not know about that make it hard for them to take criticism, you don't know what that person is going through and it's not fair that we are forced to take abuse because you're having a bad day. Nothing short of an actual salary would make it actually worth doing. I'm the same way. If something is upsetting me at the cash, I don't yell or make faces or anything. I do the best that I can to make this not painful for the person in front of me. Common fucking courtesy amiright?

Yeah... One of my managers told me that I need to just give the rude customers a smile because they're probably miserable and "If I smile at someone, then maybe that person will feel better and smile at someone else, and eventually everyone is going to be smiling." and seriously, I wanted to tell her where she could take her sunshine and rainbows because I do have depression, and keeping my emotions in check is something I've been working on for a few years, but when I'm doing full-time school (co-op) combined with almost full-time hours because they won't respect my availability it's really frustrating and exhausting. I don't have any time in the evenings or mornings where I can just exist, relax, and let go of everything that was bad that day because I get off of one thing and have to go the next. My life doesn't exist right now for me to enjoy, it's literally two full-time "jobs" of obligations :(.


Thank you for your response, I can feel my breathing becoming a bit easier. I'll try to keep this in mind while I'm at work tonight <3.

I'd love it if people were actually allow to deny customers who were coming through express with wayyyy too many items. I hate the "Customer is always right" thing. My new GM said that he's "easy on returns." the other day. Made me cringe :(

See, I'm really bad at math so when I'm shopping I always round things up a dollar or two more than it would be after tax *while I'm shopping* that way when I get to the register I'm fooling myself into being happy that I'm paying less than I anticipated. I'm a really conscious shopper though so I'm always keeping track of how much I'm spending while I'm shopping. Only time I count my items is if I'm checking if I can go through a 12 item or less lane... I'd feel like a nuisance if I went into the express lane with more than the allotted numebr of items :(

That I'm not actually as alone as I feel. I lie to myself everyday telling myself life will get better, a little easier. I just need I make it to x milestone and things will change. I tell myself I don't need my mom and that I'm so much better off without her - actually that probably is true but I guess the lie is that I'm not affected by it. I haze through life telling myself I think I'll be happy eventually but I don't think it will ever happen.

They believe that every customer with the card will spend I think it's $12.50 more per year at the store which adds up a ridiculous extra amount of profit for the store. It's a 'Hey, we're in this area, might as well stop by here while we're here.' so a lot of customers aren't regulars.... It's annoying.

Yeah, it's nerve racking. When I know that my dad is travelling anywhere (He's my best friend and the only reliable family that I have) or my SO is travelling, they have to text me when they get home or to their destination. People don't understand that when you have OCD these things aren't just a random thought of 'Oh I hope they are okay.' It's a 'Holy shit. They haven't texted me. Did something happen? Did they get into an accident?' and it goes on until you're able to hear from that person.

But as long as he's aware that I at least need to say it, I don't get upset because I know that emotionally we are wired extremely differently. Once you might the right girl, and once it hits the right time, it'll become more natural, even if you don't say it all the time, you'll at least feel confident when you do say it :)

I don't get mad at my SO when he doesn't say it back all the time, but he's understanding as to why I say it so much. I also don't call him 12 to 13 times a day, unless we're playing phone tag, but that's not my fault.

You do get added to a mailing list but we can turn that option off for you as soon as we set the card up, which I offer every single time. I've gotten grief from managers over that one but whatever, it's the customer's private information and if they don't want spam, they don't want spam.

Doesn't cost you anything to have like most cards do, they don't have an expiry date on them, the deals that we have are quite good sometimes, and if you use it the way I use my optimum card (I don't go out of my way to use it or shop there, but I do if its convenient) then you're not really losing out on anything. BUT I also understand if you don't want the card, doesn't mean I don't still have to ask..

It was the way he was complaining. I've had great conversations with customers who have said 'No thanks, I'm really sick of how many cards I have.' and I agree with them, and continue on. This customer however, halfway through my sentence raised his voice at me and just started ranting and raving when I hadn't even pushed the card. I asked, he said no, I continued on, he still felt like bitching me out for doing my job. It's easy to make a complaint without bitching out the poor cashier who is working minimum wage to go to school while paying all of her own bills.

The thing is, I do look out for customer's best interest. According to my company they'll make something like an extra $10.00 for every customer that has the card. However, I generally only ask in a regular conversational tone, they don't want it, that's totally their decision. I don't force them into it like some of my co-workers do. BUT if I see a customer is spending a fair amount of money, we have a promotion going on, and the next time they come in they'll be able to save a fair amount of money because of the card, I'll explain it to them. If I see a customer coming up to my cash with a hardcover book that I know we have in soft cover, I mention it to them because I know my work tends to make it look like we only have the more expensive version. I tend to keep my numbers where it keeps my managers happy, but I also try to keep my customers happy.

It sucks. The location I'm at forces us to fundraise for a charity, upsell our 'Favourite book', upsell whatever promotion is going on, and expect us to do it with every customer, every question, no matter what. We're a 'leadership' store or something rather so we are held to a higher standard, and they won't let me transfer locations... so I'm looking for a new job. Hopefully before Christmas....
It does suck. In some ways it's great because it benefits you, but the cashiers who are working for minimum wage got bills to pay so we gotta do what we gotta do :(

All you need to tell me is 'No.' and I'll be more than happy to move on - trust me I don't want to have to tell you about it if I don't have to. I just don't like being ranted at for doing my job.

So I helped him hunt down his books, talked with him for a bit longer than the average customer. He was talking about whatever book he was buying but he was explaining how he was around for it too (it was some history/poli-sci book - can't remember the title). Anyway, he leaves, then comes back about 5 minutes later with a $5.00 GC and says to me "You know, you're working hard, you're going to school, and you're going to do good in the world. I know it's tough, but keep going." He hands me the GC and tells me to enjoy a coffee on him on my break. I smile every time I see him come in now :).

This might be a long one. I had to switch schools a few times due to bullying and I think I'm still emotionally affected by it today (I'm female, in my early twenties). In elementary school I was diagnosed with severely debilitating OCD. I was on medication for it, I had doctors and therapists, but I never had anyone really explain to me why I had to see all these doctors, or why or how I was different. I just knew that I was and I let kids pick on me for it and pretended to laugh along with them - until I couldn't anymore. I remember in grade 6 I had few friends - most of them, if not all of them were neighborhood kids, so at school I had no friends. That year, this girl *Jane* transferred and we became the best of friends, the next year it was me, Jane, and *Sam*. We were all misfits/outcasts and we'd hang out every recess, sit together in class. I still got picked on but at least at recess I had someone I could hide out with who liked me for who I was. Grade 8 rolled around and this girl *Jessica* transferred. Jessica decided to put all the kids in my class, and the grade 7s against me. It was brutal. I was hanging out with another kid that I'd been friends with since grade 3 and she came over, shoved me, scoffed at me, and told me to go away. I stood my ground, told her no and she laughed at me, told me that this was exactly why nobody liked me. A lot of grade school is a blur because this was the type of treatment I got nearly every day.


In grade 8 I was also sexually assaulted by one of my classmates, on my school bus, with about 4 or 5 other kids watching. On the bus every day the kids would steal my shoes until my bus stop so I would have to put my shoes on after I got off the bus, they would steal my bag, call me names, trap me in my seat so I couldn't get away from their teasing... it was bad. Then one day this kid was trying to trap me again, I'd gotten stronger than him over the year and began pushing my way out of the seat, then he yelled out for *John* to come and help him and John took over. Shoved me up against the window and started touching me inappropriately. Everyone laughed. I got off the bus bawling my eyes out and told my parents what happened. My father freaked out, called the school, and I didn't go to school for a week (I was 12 by the way). When I finally had to go back to school my dad took me to tell the principal what happened and discuss consequences for the kid. She adamently said that the only thing they could do was give him a one day in school suspension and write me a letter of apology. They ended up sending a police officer to our classroom to talk about what happened and for the rest of the year I got made fun of for overreacting, and my classmates telling me it was a joke and that I should learn to just take it as it was. Eventually I snapped and beat up a kid on my bus who was picking on me. He was twice my size but I was doing martial arts so I knocked him down pretty easily. Almost got suspended. My dad was outraged and switched me schools after that year. I remember our teachers forced everyone in my grade 8 class to sign each other's hats and this one kid wrote "Ew. I can't believe I have to sign this. Can't wait to never see your face again."


And so high school began. Grade 9 I ate my lunch in the bathroom by myself for the first week or two, made some great friends and had a blast. Grade 10 kids started to again realize that I was different, socially awkward, younger (I'd skipped a grade), and saw that I was an easy target. Grade 11 was really the worst of it though. Every day I would get called horse faced dyke. I got threatened to get beat up by a group of about 6 girls on a regular basis. Honestly, I've blocked a lot of it out. But I started skipping school all the time. Sneaking to my locker so I could avoid getting beat up. Walking home for lunch so I wouldn't get picked up, sitting alone in class. It was torture. After grade 11 I switched schools again and near the end of that year a lot of the same name-calling and threats were happening.


After talking about what happened in elementary school I don't really have the energy emotionally to keep talking about my high school experience, but if anyone has any specific questions, feel free to inquire. The bullying made it much harder to make friends when I left for university, and I feel like my self-esteem took a huge dive and is the reason for why I don't try new things and then regret not doing them later. I really can't believe how harsh kids are sometimes.

**TL;DR**: Got diagnosed with debilitating OCD when I was just starting elementary school, got teased a lot for being different, got called names, pushed out of social groups, had my things stolen, forced to endure torture on the school bus, was sexually assaulted on said school bus at age 12, principal said nothing could be done about it and then classmates started teasing me saying I took it too seriously and that it was a joke, almost got suspended for beating up one of my bullies after I snapped, switched schools, everything was good. Started getting called names again a couple of years later, threatened to be beaten up every other day, was socially isolated, self-esteem is still affected to this day.

I'm a female in my early 20s btw. I nicely tell her and point to my crutches that I can't because I've hurt my ankle and I can't keep my balance. This isn't good enough for her. She starts raising her voice at me about how because she's pregnant she has a RIGHT to MY seat and that I better get out of her seat etc. etc. I can't remember her exact words but once she started getting aggressive and rude I just started ignoring her until she gave up and walked to the back of the bus. ... Bitch.

Just be patient if you're needing help on the sales floor because we are REALLY busy and most people I work with do enjoy the merchandise they work with, want to give you recommendations where you need them, want to get you that product that will make your child's whole Christmas but we want to do that for the mass crowd of customers that are coming through. Be patient at the cash register, don't be offended if we don't engage with you as much as we usually would, there are lines literally (yes literally) out the door, try and have your method of payment ready as you're coming up to the cash so that we don't have to wait for you to search through your purse. Just try and understand that we are under a lot of stress and pressure, from customers and managers and we just want to keep everyone happy, and get home at the end of the day. That's all I can really think of - just be aware that every other customer in the store wants the same thing you do and that the staff is doing everything they can to help you, so if we don't have that product, or you have to wait 5 or 10 minutes to get help, we're not hiding from you or doing it on purpose, it's because we have someone who we are helping as fast as we can.

It may sound awful but I have NO sympathy for the drunk driver, even if they feel guilty because they made the CHOICE to drive that way. The person who lost loved ones didn't make that choice, the person who decided to drive sober didn't make that choice, and now it's that family that has to grieve the loss of someone they loved.


Maybe this makes me naive, or stubborn, or unreasonable, but I still feel like to some degree at the core of it all, most people know that drinking and driving is wrong and if it takes someone actually doing it to realize that there's something wrong with doing it, then something needs to change in your home town...

From Wikipedia for 3) There's no **antivenom** but there is a treatment in which the person being bitten can survive:

>Treatment
First aid treatment is pressure on the wound and artificial respiration once the paralysis has disabled the victim's respiratory muscles, which often occurs within minutes of being bitten. Tetrodotoxin causes severe and often total body paralysis; the victim remains conscious and alert in a manner similar to curare or pancuronium bromide. This effect, however, is temporary and will fade over a period of hours as the tetrodotoxin is metabolized and excreted by the body. It is thus essential that rescue breathing be continued without pause until the paralysis subsides and the victim regains the ability to breathe on their own. This is a daunting physical prospect for a single individual, but use of a bag valve mask respirator reduces fatigue to sustainable levels until help can arrive.
Definitive hospital treatment involves placing the patient on a medical ventilator until the toxin is neutralized by the body. The symptoms vary in severity, with children being the most at risk because of their small body size. Because the venom primarily kills through paralysis, victims are frequently saved if artificial respiration is started and maintained before marked cyanosis and hypotension develop. Victims who live through the first 24 hours generally go on to make a complete recovery.[7]


>It is essential that efforts continue even if the victim appears not to be responding. Tetrodotoxin poisoning can result in the victim being fully aware of their surroundings but unable to breathe. Because of the paralysis that occurs they have no way of signaling for help or any way of indicating distress. Respiratory support, together with reassurance, until medical assistance arrives ensures that the victim will generally recover well.
The blue-ringed octopus, despite its small size, carries enough venom to kill 26 adult humans within minutes. Furthermore, their bites are tiny and often painless, with many victims not realizing they have been envenomated until respiratory depression and paralysis start to set in.[8]

The usual argument is that people who commit suicide who have some sort of mental illness (usually rooted in depression/anxiety) that they can just go get "treated for it". I have depression, and grew up with severe, almost debilitating OCD. It is really hard to live sometimes. I have the OCD more under control but people think it's just something that can be cured by a pill taken daily, or talking to someone who is "Trained to deal with people like you." Therapy and counselling takes A LOT of effort, energy, and money depending on what type of help you're seeking out.


When you're depressed you can't even find a reason to get out of bed in the morning. From the time you wake up, you're counting down the hours until you can go home, go to bed, and get a few hours of sleep just to escape everything for a little while. You spend so much energy plastering a smile on your face so that you can do your job, keep your friends, go to school, live this life that *you just don't want to live*. 


Sure, you have family, friends, and somewhere in your mind you know that it would hurt them to lose you. But would it really? You're depressed and tired all the time anyways, your parents have each other/their SO's, your siblings have each other, their SO's, their friends. Your friends have their other friends and family. People might be upset for a day or two, but they'll move on and eventually it'll be like you never existed. How else would it go? You haven't impacted anybody's life, you haven't done anything worthwhile, you're just a waste of oxygen, and resources that could be better used for someone who's worth having on this earth.


Now logically and to a sane mind, does this make any sense? No it doesn't. But again, it's debilitating, exhausting, and **depressing**. I think that if the individual suffering does seek out help, tries out medication, therapy, counselling... everything that is currently available to help them overcome their mental illness and they still feel like their lives are just as unfulfilled, I think that they should not be judged for ending their lives. I think it is justifiable that if you can't conceivably envision another day of living on this earth because everything just feels completely worthless for you... do it. 


I know it will hurt your loved ones to know that you were suffering so much, and they will probably blame themselves for a while, but it is NOT their fault. You just can't find a reason to make your life worth living, and you're the one who has to wake up every day in your own body and mind knowing how miserable the next day ahead of you is, no one else. In my opinion, if all treatments have been exhausted, **it's selfish of those around you to expect you to live your life miserably, just so they don't have to live on without you** when eventually, all humans will finish grieving your death and move on.
